title: MSP Mac Help Desk Guru (work from home)
description: Headquarters: ignitionit.com URL: https://ignitionit.com Fully Remote · Work from home · Full-time (Eastern or Pacific time zones) · Apple-first TL;DR ignitionit.com is a seasoned, Apple-first MSP — in business for almost 30 years — and we're hiring a Help Desk Technician to be the friendly, capable first voice our clients reach when something isn't working. This position is a remote, work-from-home, full-time role. We've written this as a junior-to-mid-level job description because that's where most great people start on our team. But if you're more seasoned — comfortable in identity, MDM, or security work — don't scroll past. We'd be delighted to find someone who can step in higher up the ladder, and we'll happily talk about a more senior scope and comp if that's you. What the actual job??? Unlike many IT shops, we believe that the technology is the tactic. The actual job is making people feel taken care of. One of our core values is “49% tech support, 51% human support.” You'll succeed by configuring devices, resetting access, untangling email, and chasing down the gremlin that's been haunting someone's conference room. But you'll know you succeeded when a client exhales and says, “Thank goodness you're on it!” That Warm Fuzzy Feeling™ is the actual product. The green lights on the dashboard are just how we get there. In a typical week, you might: Onboard a new hire at a fast-growing startup: provision their Mac, set up their Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 accounts, enroll the device in MDM, and make sure day one feels effortless. Offboard a departing employee cleanly — recover the laptop, revoke access, and close the loop so nothing's left dangling. All boxes checked, ticket notated and closed, client followed up with. Field a "my email stopped working" ticket that turns out to be a DNS thing, a phishing-filter thing, or a "they changed their password on their phone three weeks ago" thing. Help a family office or RIA get a touchy Zoom Room or conference-room AV setup behaving before a meeting — over the phone. Triage the queue so phones get answered fast, emails don't rot, and nobody feels forgotten — even when the honest answer is, “We're on it, but here's the realistic timeline." ⠀ You'll be the front line: helping with what you can, researching what you can't, and pinging the rest of the team when you're genuinely stuck. That last part is a skill, not a weakness — knowing when to ask is half the job. About ignitionit.com We're one of the oldest Apple Technical Partners on the planet, and one of the only certified Apple Premier Partners — that’s kinda like getting knighted by the ghost of Steve Jobs. We started where you’d expect to find Macs (creative agencies, non-profits, education) but our primary clients today are cutting-edge, venture-backed AI SaaS startups, VC and private equity firms, registered investment advisors — many of them operating under stringent compliance expectations (SOC 2, SEC). That means we hold ourselves to a higher standard than the scrappy shop we started as. Polished, reliable, security-minded work is the baseline now — but always with a smile! What hasn't changed: relationships are still our most valuable currency — with clients, with vendors, and with each other. We're a tight, supportive team. We teach each other what we know, cover for each other when life throws a punch, and care a little too much about doing things the right way. We're still a bit weird, and our clients seem to like us that way. We move fast, priorities shift, it’s not always documented (whatever it is), our tool set and list of supported platforms is sprawling, and some days the to-do list is longer than you'd like. If you can stay warm under pressure, create order out of chaos, learn new stuff fast because you love it, and speak up when you need help, you'll thrive here. If you need a rigid, fully-documented, never-changes environment where nobody trusts you with admin access, where you will be micro-managed so you never have to wonder whether or not you’re doing the right thing, this isn't it. You’ll have a ton of independence on our team, and freedom to use your best judgment to get the ball over the finish line, but that also means we expect you to be naturally responsible, honest, and highly accountable — to yourself, your teammates, and the clients. As they say, the price of freedom is eternal vigilance. The tech you'll work with (and grow into) Day one, you'll be living in: Apple at the core — macOS, iOS, Apple Business Manager, and MDM (Jamf / Iru / Intune / Workspace ONE / and more) Yes, PCs too — about one-third of our users are driving Windows Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 admin consoles Identity and access — SSO, MFA, and security keys (Okta, Entra ID, Yubikey, and friends) Lots of other security tools — our stack is constantly evolving and may vary from client to client The everyday productivity stack — Slack, Zoom, conference-room AV, networking basics (Meraki), and endpoint tooling ⠀ You don't need to know all of this. You need to be the kind of person who wants to. As you grow, there's a clear path into infrastructure administration, project architecture and implementation, and — for the right person — security and compliance work (phishing simulations, endpoint detection, SOC 2 / CIS / SEC readiness, due diligence questionnaire support, etc.). That's where our most senior people live, and it's wide open. Who we hope you are The hard requirements — we won't move forward unless you: Can work standard business hours in Eastern or Pacific time zones (we currently need both) Have a quiet home workspace and reliable broadband Have proven Apple aptitude — you actually use and like the Apple ecosystem Have at least 5 years of IT support experience on the job. ⠀ Everything else — and this is the longer list, on purpose. We figure technical skills are teachable; character takes a lot longer. So we're looking for someone who: Genuinely cares — about clients, teammates, and doing right by people Loves to learn, and proves it in how they spend their time Reads, and writes clearly — clear writing is clear thinking, and you'll do a lot of it Stays calm and kind with a frustrated person on the other end of the line Can tell the difference between good customer service and fantastic customer service, and refuses to settle for the former Notices when something's being done inefficiently and fixes it (you may boast about it later, that’s fine) Proofreads their own work (yes, we noticed whether you proofread your application) Has a sense of humor, and doesn't take themselves too seriously Regarding AI Our company founder/CEO is headquartered in the Bay Area. We work with innovative, ambitious companies developing AI products. Our team members hold a range of opinions about whether AI is “good or bad” for humans, but at the end of the day, we embrace the plain fact that it is here, we must embrace it to evolve, and our clients increasingly depend on us to help them embrace it, too, to help them evolve and stay competitive. Our CEO's opinion: AI will not replace human labor any time soon; rather, AI is a new opportunity to either (a) get things done faster, or (b) get a much higher quality of output than before. If you’re an AI tinkerer, great! We want to hear how you’re using it and see your latest vibe project. If you’re allergic to AI or have no interest in learning new habits to work effectively with it, this is not the place for you. Compensation & logistics Base salary: Applicants outside the USA will be compensated according to your local employment market. For applicants closer to the junior side who are located in the USA, $50,000–$65,000/yr, depending on experience level and your local geographical price index. With experience, comp goes up from there. Genuinely experienced, more senior candidates can be slotted higher — let's talk. Type & location: Full-time, work from home, fully remote. Eastern or Pacific time zones. Benefits: Medical / dental / vision for the employee, 401(k) with employer contribution, 2 weeks of PTO annually to start, and a stipend for your home internet. raw.description:
Headquarters: ignitionit.com
URL: https://ignitionit.com

Fully Remote · Work from home · Full-time (Eastern or Pacific time zones) · Apple-first 

TL;DR

ignitionit.com is a seasoned, Apple-first MSP — in business for almost 30 years — and we're hiring a Help Desk Technician to be the friendly, capable first voice our clients reach when something isn't working. This position is a remote, work-from-home, full-time role.

We've written this as a junior-to-mid-level job description because that's where most great people start on our team. But if you're more seasoned — comfortable in identity, MDM, or security work — don't scroll past. We'd be delighted to find someone who can step in higher up the ladder, and we'll happily talk about a more senior scope and comp if that's you.

What the actual job???

Unlike many IT shops, we believe that the technology is the tactic. The actual job is making people feel taken care of. One of our core values is “49% tech support, 51% human support.”

You'll succeed by configuring devices, resetting access, untangling email, and chasing down the gremlin that's been haunting someone's conference room. But you'll know you succeeded when a client exhales and says, “Thank goodness you're on it!” That Warm Fuzzy Feeling™ is the actual product. The green lights on the dashboard are just how we get there.

In a typical week, you might:

  • Onboard a new hire at a fast-growing startup: provision their Mac, set up their Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 accounts, enroll the device in MDM, and make sure day one feels effortless.

  • Offboard a departing employee cleanly — recover the laptop, revoke access, and close the loop so nothing's left dangling. All boxes checked, ticket notated and closed, client followed up with.

  • Field a "my email stopped working" ticket that turns out to be a DNS thing, a phishing-filter thing, or a "they changed their password on their phone three weeks ago" thing.

  • Help a family office or RIA get a touchy Zoom Room or conference-room AV setup behaving before a meeting — over the phone.

  • Triage the queue so phones get answered fast, emails don't rot, and nobody feels forgotten — even when the honest answer is, “We're on it, but here's the realistic timeline."

⠀ You'll be the front line: helping with what you can, researching what you can't, and pinging the rest of the team when you're genuinely stuck. That last part is a skill, not a weakness — knowing when to ask is half the job.

About ignitionit.com

We're one of the oldest Apple Technical Partners on the planet, and one of the only certified Apple Premier Partners — that’s kinda like getting knighted by the ghost of Steve Jobs. We started where you’d expect to find Macs (creative agencies, non-profits, education) but our primary clients today are cutting-edge, venture-backed AI SaaS startups, VC and private equity firms, registered investment advisors — many of them operating under stringent compliance expectations (SOC 2, SEC). That means we hold ourselves to a higher standard than the scrappy shop we started as. Polished, reliable, security-minded work is the baseline now — but always with a smile!

What hasn't changed: relationships are still our most valuable currency — with clients, with vendors, and with each other. We're a tight, supportive team. We teach each other what we know, cover for each other when life throws a punch, and care a little too much about doing things the right way. We're still a bit weird, and our clients seem to like us that way.

We move fast, priorities shift, it’s not always documented (whatever it is), our tool set and list of supported platforms is sprawling, and some days the to-do list is longer than you'd like. If you can stay warm under pressure, create order out of chaos, learn new stuff fast because you love it, and speak up when you need help, you'll thrive here.

If you need a rigid, fully-documented, never-changes environment where nobody trusts you with admin access, where you will be micro-managed so you never have to wonder whether or not you’re doing the right thing, this isn't it. You’ll have a ton of independence on our team, and freedom to use your best judgment to get the ball over the finish line, but that also means we expect you to be naturally responsible, honest, and highly accountable — to yourself, your teammates, and the clients. As they say, the price of freedom is eternal vigilance.

The tech you'll work with (and grow into)

Day one, you'll be living in:

  • Apple at the core — macOS, iOS, Apple Business Manager, and MDM (Jamf / Iru / Intune / Workspace ONE / and more)

  • Yes, PCs too — about one-third of our users are driving Windows

  • Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 admin consoles

  • Identity and access — SSO, MFA, and security keys (Okta, Entra ID, Yubikey, and friends)

  • Lots of other security tools — our stack is constantly evolving and may vary from client to client

  • The everyday productivity stack — Slack, Zoom, conference-room AV, networking basics (Meraki), and endpoint tooling

⠀ You don't need to know all of this. You need to be the kind of person who wants to. As you grow, there's a clear path into infrastructure administration, project architecture and implementation, and — for the right person — security and compliance work (phishing simulations, endpoint detection, SOC 2 / CIS / SEC readiness, due diligence questionnaire support, etc.). That's where our most senior people live, and it's wide open.

Who we hope you are

The hard requirements — we won't move forward unless you:

  • Can work standard business hours in Eastern or Pacific time zones (we currently need both)

  • Have a quiet home workspace and reliable broadband

  • Have proven Apple aptitude — you actually use and like the Apple ecosystem

  • Have at least 5 years of IT support experience on the job. 

⠀ Everything else — and this is the longer list, on purpose. We figure technical skills are teachable; character takes a lot longer. So we're looking for someone who:

  • Genuinely cares — about clients, teammates, and doing right by people

  • Loves to learn, and proves it in how they spend their time

  • Reads, and writes clearly — clear writing is clear thinking, and you'll do a lot of it

  • Stays calm and kind with a frustrated person on the other end of the line

  • Can tell the difference between good customer service and fantastic customer service, and refuses to settle for the former

  • Notices when something's being done inefficiently and fixes it (you may boast about it later, that’s fine)

  • Proofreads their own work (yes, we noticed whether you proofread your application)

  • Has a sense of humor, and doesn't take themselves too seriously

Regarding AI

Our company founder/CEO is headquartered in the Bay Area. We work with innovative, ambitious companies developing AI products. Our team members hold a range of opinions about whether AI is “good or bad” for humans, but at the end of the day, we embrace the plain fact that it is here, we must embrace it to evolve, and our clients increasingly depend on us to help them embrace it, too, to help them evolve and stay competitive.

Our CEO's opinion: AI will not replace human labor any time soon; rather, AI is a new opportunity to either (a) get things done faster, or (b) get a much higher quality of output than before. If you’re an AI tinkerer, great! We want to hear how you’re using it and see your latest vibe project. If you’re allergic to AI or have no interest in learning new habits to work effectively with it, this is not the place for you.

Compensation & logistics

  • Base salary: Applicants outside the USA will be compensated according to your local employment market. For applicants closer to the junior side who are located in the USA, $50,000–$65,000/yr, depending on experience level and your local geographical price index. With experience, comp goes up from there. Genuinely experienced, more senior candidates can be slotted higher — let's talk. 

  • Type & location: Full-time, work from home, fully remote. Eastern or Pacific time zones.

  • Benefits: Medical / dental / vision for the employee, 401(k) with employer contribution, 2 weeks of PTO annually to start, and a stipend for your home internet.

How to apply

The first step is really easy and only takes 10 minutes — no resume, no cover letter, no essays. Here's how:

  1. Take this online Culture Index assessment (about 10 minutes): We use it to screen for people whose natural wiring fits how our team works.

  2. If your profile lines up with what we're looking for, we'll reach out and ask you to complete a 60-minute TestGorilla assessment for critical thinking skills, send us your resume, and maybe a couple of other items.

  3. From there, we conduct between 2-4 video interviews. One of these might be a live technical assessment.

If the Culture Index step feels like a strange way to start a job application — that's kind of the point. Remember the phrase Think Different?

Ignition is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and will consider all qualified applicants. Good luck in your search — and may the Force be with you!

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/ignition-inc-msp-mac-help-desk-guru-work-from-home

description: Headquarters: San Francisco Bay Area or Remote (U.S.) Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games. We are seeking a QA/DevOps Engineer to join Discord’s Business Systems team. In this role, you will own automated test suite development and maintenance across Oracle ERP Cloud (Fusion) and Salesforce, with a focus on Tosca-based regression and progression testing. You will embed automated testing into CI/CD pipelines and partner closely with ERP Functional, Technical, and DevOps teams to ensure every release is tested consistently and defects are caught early. What you'll be doing Run Oracle ERP Cloud and Salesforce QA automation suites for all quarterly patch upgrades end-to-end. Review new Oracle and SFDC release features and recommend improvements to existing testing processes. Build and improve regression and progression test automation in the Tosca environment for Oracle Fusion and Salesforce. Create, maintain, and update Tosca scripts to reflect system and process changes across GL, AP, AR, and FAH modules. Lead feature enhancement reviews as part of quarterly patch assessment cycles and new enhancement projects. Integrate automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines; trigger regression suites automatically on every release candidate build. Maintain test infrastructure and environments in collaboration with DevOps and ERP Technical teams. Document test coverage, defect trends, and release readiness in Jira and shared reporting dashboards. Automation Use Cases FAH Process Automation: Auto-test Financial Accounting Hub on each new sales item addition to eliminate manual unit testing. AR Regression Suite: Automated flows for invoicing, receipts, and customer setup across every release. AP Regression Suite: Payment runs, supplier invoices, holds, and approvals tested automatically on each patch cycle. Salesforce Tosca Automation: Develop, maintain, and expand automated SFDC test suites in Tosca, integrated with release pipelines. What you should have 3-5+ years of QA automation experience. Hands-on Tosca experience for regression and progression test suite development and maintenance. Experience executing and maintaining automated test cycles for quarterly Oracle patch upgrades. Familiarity with Oracle ERP Cloud and SFDC release feature review and technical impact assessment. Experience integrating automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or equivalent). Familiarity with pipeline configuration: triggering regression runs on pull requests and release candidate builds. Working knowledge of version control (Git / GitHub or GitLab): branching, pull requests, and code review workflows. Basic scripting capability in Python, Shell, or PowerShell for test utility automation and pipeline support. Understanding of containerized test environments (Docker); experience running tests in ephemeral containers is a plus. Jira for defect tracking, test coverage reporting, and sprint participation. Experience writing and maintaining test documentation: test plans, test cases, regression logs, and release readiness summaries. Ability to work cross-functionally with ERP Functional Analysts, ERP Technical Developers, and DevOps engineers. Familiarity with SOX compliance, ITGC controls, and ERP change management practices. Preferred Qualifications Oracle Fusion certification or formal training in Oracle ERP Cloud modules. Experience with SaaS QA automation in a high-growth technology company environment. Exposure to OIC (Oracle Integration Cloud) or MuleSoft integration testing. Familiarity with Salesforce test automation frameworks beyond Tosca (Selenium, Provar, or equivalent). Prior experience working with AMS or managed services vendors in an ERP context. Knowledge of Oracle quarterly release cycles and technical impact assessments. Exposure to infrastructure-as-code or environment provisioning concepts (Terraform, Ansible). This position is US-based and can be remote but if you live in the Bay Area, you’re welcome to work from our beautiful SF office. The base salary range for this full-time position is listed below. This position will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in role postings reflect the base salary only, and do not include equity, or benefits. Base Salary $156,000 — $175,500 USD Why Discord? Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming. We're a multiplatform, multigenerational and multiplayer platform that helps people deepen their friendships around games and shared interests, and helps developers build and grow their businesses. We believe games give us a way to have fun with our favorite people, whether listening to music together or grinding in competitive matches for diamond rank. Join us in our mission! Your future is just a click away! Discord is committed to inclusion and providing reasonable accommodations during the interview process. We want you to feel set up for success, so if you are in need of reasonable accommodations, please let your recruiter know. Please see our Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy for details regarding Discord’s collection and usage of personal information relating to the application and recruitment process by clicking HERE. title: Channel Account Manager
description: Headquarters: USA - Remote About Ping Identity: At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it. Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. We are seeking a strategic, field-facing Channel Account Manager to lead channels for Ping’s Enterprise team. Ping’s Enterprise sales team is the new-logo engine for companies with less than $2B in revenue and spans the commercial segment of the USA. This team has a track record of exceeding targets, and your role will help them to work with partners to drive a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You will spend meaningful time in the field with partner and Ping sales teams, building rep-to-rep engagement and turning joint account plans into qualified pipeline and closed business. You will also help organize regional partner engagements that bring the right teams together around target accounts and repeatable go-to-market plays. This is a builder role for someone who is thoughtful, positive, curious, and ready to turn strategy into action. You Will: Own the Enterprise partner strategy and plan, with a clear focus on new-logo acquisition, regional coverage, partner priorities, and measurable outcomes. Build trusted relationships with partner executives, alliance leaders, sellers, technical teams, and delivery organizations, while working in the field with partners and Ping sales teams to identify target accounts and create joint account plans. Drive rep-to-rep engagement between Ping sellers and partner sellers, helping teams identify opportunities, coordinate pursuits, and progress new-logo deals. Set up and support regional partner events, including field meetings, account-mapping sessions, enablements, workshops, roundtables, and other activities designed to create partner-to-partner engagement and qualified pipeline. Develop repeatable partner go-to-market plays and practical enablement that help partners position Ping Identity, engage new enterprise accounts, and progress opportunities. Partner with Enterprise sales, Partner Solutions Engineering, marketing, services, and product teams to remove friction and help partners win and deliver successfully. Track partner activity, event engagement, sourced and influenced pipeline, new-logo progress, and follow-through; use the data to focus time and investment where it will have the greatest impact. Deliver measurable impact by expanding productive partner coverage, increasing partner-led new-logo pipeline, improving rep-to-rep engagement, and turning regional activity into repeatable growth. You Have: 10+ years of experience in channel, alliances, partner sales, or a related go-to-market role in enterprise technology. Experience working with partners to acquire new customers and build sourced or influenced pipeline in the Enterprise market. Experience managing or developing relationships with integrators, resellers, delivery partners, and/or distributors. A track record of building partner programs, joint account plans, field motions, or other repeatable go-to-market plays—not simply managing existing relationships. Strong field presence and the ability to engage credibly with partner executives, sellers, technical teams, and Ping sales leaders. Excellent communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to create productive rep-to-rep conversations and turn meetings into clear next steps. A positive, practical, and collaborative approach; you create momentum, follow through on commitments, and are comfortable operating in a changing environment. Willingness to travel regularly and spend meaningful time with partners, customers, and internal teams in the field. Bonus Points If You Have: Experience in cybersecurity, identity and access management, or another complex enterprise technology category. Experience working with both national and regional partners, or building partner coverage in new territories. Experience planning and executing regional partner events, roundtables, workshops, or field marketing programs. Experience creating partner enablement programs, certifications, technical workshops, or sales plays. Experience working with sales development, account executives, and partner sellers to create net-new opportunities. Enthusiasm for representing the company at partner forums, industry events, roundtables, and other public-facing engagements. A relevant degree or equivalent experience, and/or cybersecurity or channel-related certifications. Salary Range: $88,000–$132,000 base + Commission In accordance with Colorado’s Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (SB 19-085) the approximate compensation range for this role in Colorado is listed above. Final compensation for this role will be determined by various factors, such as knowledge, skills, and abilities. Life at Ping: We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day. Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special: A company culture that empowers you to do your best work. Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone. Regular company and team bonding events. Competitive benefits and perks. Global volunteering and community initiatives Our Benefits: Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule Parental Leave Progressive Healthcare Options Retirement Programs Opportunity for Education Reimbursement Commuter Offset (Specific locations) Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self. We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch.

What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership
  • Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)
  • Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance
  • Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards
  • Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires
  • Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, executive communication, and post-incident learning
  • Represent Carrot's security posture to employers, health plans, and health systems through security reviews, questionnaires, and strategic sales conversations
  • Work with Legal and Privacy to meet global data protection requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) for member health data
  • Build, coach, and grow the security team, balancing hands-on execution with delegation as the team scales
  • Manage the security budget, tooling, and vendor relationships, and tailor security guidance for a remote-first workforce and physical offices

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • A documented, executive-endorsed security strategy and multi-year roadmap with clear priorities, owners, and measures of progress
  • Clean outcomes on recurring audits and certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS), with remediation items closed on schedule
  • A tested incident response program, with regular tabletop exercises completed and lessons learned built back into the program
  • A measurable reduction in high-risk vulnerabilities and open security findings, with remediation timelines agreed on with Engineering
  • A living risk register and vendor security review process that leaders rely on to make decisions
  • A security team with defined roles, clear growth paths, and the right capacity for Carrot's growth, including key hires made
  • Faster, more consistent security reviews for Sales and Customer Success, with fewer escalations from enterprise customers
  • A clear plan, and visible progress, on any additional frameworks the business prioritizes, such as ISO 27001

About You

You likely have:

  • A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 10+ years of experience in technology, including 5+ years in information security and at least 3 years leading security teams
  • A security certification such as CISSP or CISM
  • Experience leading the security function at a late-stage startup, scale-up, or public company
  • Working depth in healthcare data protection and privacy frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA
  • Experience overseeing enterprise frameworks and audits such as SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001
  • Strong knowledge of application, network, and cloud security (AWS and Azure) and frameworks such as NIST CSF and OWASP
  • Experience running core security programs, including incident response, risk management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security awareness
  • Executive-level communication skills and confidence engaging customers and sales teams on security requirements
  • Experience managing budget and allocating resources across people, tools, and vendors

 

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience leading security through a major company event such as an IPO, acquisition, or large-scale audit cycle
  • A background in healthcare, digital health, or another highly regulated, high-trust environment
  • Experience leading security in a remote-first, globally distributed company
  • Familiarity with compliance automation platforms such as Drata
  • Experience building a security engineering practice alongside platform and infrastructure teams

 

Why This Role Matters

Members trust Carrot with some of the most personal information a person can share, often during some of the most meaningful moments of their lives. Protecting that trust is not a back-office function. It is what allows employers, health plans, and health systems to bring Carrot to millions of people worldwide.

As Carrot grows, security leadership shapes how we build, how we sell, and how we show up for customers. In this role, you will make security a strength that members and customers can see and rely on, and build a team that keeps raising the bar as the business scales.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $188,000.00 - $245,000.00. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience.

description: Headquarters: Portugal - Remote Be Part of Building the Future Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Learn more at www.dremio.com. About the role Dremio's Connectivity team builds the high-performance connectivity solutions that help customers bring data to Dremio and connect Dremio to the broader data ecosystem. The team works across client drivers, protocols, connectors, interoperability, distributed systems, and the reliability and supportability of production data access. As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll independently own multiple medium-to-large features or service components within a Connectivity and Clients area. You'll define the approach for a substantial team-area scope, turn ambiguous goals into clear milestones, make sound feature and service-level design decisions, and drive work through reliable production delivery. You will bring deep expertise in at least one area, such as JDBC or ODBC drivers, Apache Arrow ADBC, Arrow Flight SQL, BI interoperability, source connectivity, or connectivity reliability, while contributing effectively across adjacent areas. You will also mentor engineers and influence partner teams through strong technical judgment and execution. What you'll be doing Own substantial connectivity work: Lead multiple medium-to-large features or service components from problem definition through design, implementation, validation, release readiness, and operational handoff. Turn ambiguity into an execution plan: Define reviewable milestones, acceptance measures, dependencies, estimates, and risks for complex customer, product, and engineering goals. Design scalable, maintainable systems: Produce technical designs and architecture diagrams, explain trade-offs, and make feature and service-level decisions across drivers, protocols, client libraries, connectors, and distributed services. Diagnose complex failures: Lead root-cause analysis across client/server, protocol, network, authentication, metadata, and distributed-system boundaries using logs, telemetry, profiles, benchmarks, and production evidence. Build compatibility and reliability: Maintain API and protocol stability; create automated compatibility, interoperability, performance, scale, reliability, observability, and diagnostics coverage; and define practical migration paths for supported and legacy clients. Collaborate and influence: Partner with Product, Query Execution, QA, Support, SRE, Documentation, and external technology partners to resolve dependencies and improve certification, customer experience, and supportability. Programming expertise: Deep proficiency in Java, C++, Rust, Go, or another systems or services language, with the ability to work effectively in adjacent languages and frameworks. Connectivity and systems depth: Experience designing and debugging APIs, protocols, client libraries, drivers, or distributed services, with strong knowledge of data structures, concurrency, asynchronous programming, networking, and failure handling. Problem-solving ability: Able to identify and solve non-obvious problems across client/server and distributed-system boundaries and turn findings into durable fixes and regression coverage. Quality mindset: Experience building comprehensive unit, integration, compatibility, performance, or reliability tests and working with production CI/CD, packaging, release, certification, and engineering quality controls. Communication and influence: Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain technical trade-offs, surface risks early, align contributors across teams, and influence without formal authority. Mentorship: Demonstrated ability to mentor and coach engineers and improve the effectiveness and engineering practices of the team around you. Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees and equivalent industry experience are welcomed. Bonus points if you have Experience developing JDBC, ODBC, ADBC, or other database drivers. Experience with Apache Arrow or Arrow Flight SQL. Experience with SQL engines, databases, data platforms, or source connectors. BI interoperability experience with Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or similar tools, including collaboration with partner engineering teams. Knowledge of OAuth, OIDC, TLS, enterprise authentication, metadata discovery, or query pushdown. Cross-platform native build, packaging, release engineering, compatibility certification, or upgrade support experience. Observability, production diagnostics, customer escalation, long-running data transfer, cancellation, keepalive, timeout, or proxy experience. title: Graduate Transport Planner
description:
At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone.

For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive.

As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career.

Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning.

What you'll be doing

You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements.

  • Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports.

  • Analysing traffic, transport and movement data.

  • Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies.

  • Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments.

  • Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

  • Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations.

  • Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects.

What kind of projects will I get to work on?

You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including:

  • Residential developments.

  • Urban regeneration schemes.

  • Commercial and industrial projects.

  • Education and healthcare developments.

  • Mixed-use masterplans.

  • Strategic land and development opportunities.

You'll help assess how developments interact with the transport network and support clients through the planning process, helping turn ideas into deliverable projects.

How will Curtins support my development?

Our goal is simple: to help you become the best engineer you can be.

Through the Curtins Graduate Academy, you'll follow a structured development programme designed to accelerate both your technical and professional growth.

You'll benefit from:

  • A structured graduate development programme.

  • Dedicated mentoring and coaching.

  • Regular technical and professional skills training.

  • Support towards professional registration and Chartership.

  • Exposure to a wide range of projects, clients and sectors.

  • Opportunities to build your network across the business.

You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are genuinely invested in your success and development.

What we're looking for

We're looking for graduates who are curious, analytical and interested in how development projects are planned and delivered.

You'll ideally be studying towards or have recently completed a degree in:

  • Transport Planning

  • Geography

  • Urban Planning

  • Civil Engineering

  • Town Planning

  • Geography or a related discipline

It would also be advantageous to hold an MSc in Transport Planning, Transport Engineering, Urban Planning, or Development Planning.

Most importantly, we're looking for people who share our values:

Integrity - Doing the right thing.

Being Human - Supporting and respecting others.

Curiosity - Asking questions and seeking better solutions.

Impact - Making a meaningful difference through our work.

Why join Curtins?

As an employee-owned business, every person at Curtins contributes to and benefits from our success.

Alongside exciting projects and a supportive culture, you'll enjoy:

  • Industry-leading benefits package.

  • Award-winning training and development programmes.

  • Employee ownership benefits.

  • Opportunities to get involved in STEM, charity and community initiatives.

  • Access to our unique Employee Extras, including our 5-star holiday lodges.

Most importantly, you'll be joining a business where your ideas matter, your development is supported and your contribution makes a real difference.

Build your future with Curtins.

Should you wish to discuss any adjustments to the application process or provide us with feedback please contact hr@curtins.com we would be happy to discuss ways we can make the process more suitable to your needs.

We value diversity and respect all differences in people. We invite enthusiastic individuals who share in our values of teamwork, client focus, integrity, and quality to apply to join us.

Please mention the word **UNRIVALED** and tag RMjAuMTY4LjExOC44Nw== when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RMjAuMTY4LjExOC44Nw==). This is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants. Companies can search these words to find applicants that read this and see they're human.

Headquarters: Remote

You're the detection engineer people turn to when they ask "what does Microsoft actually see here?" Not the marketing-slide answer, the real map. Which product emits which telemetry, any anticipated ingestion lags, what table or API it lands in, which license tier gates it, how long it survives before it ages out, and where the documentation quietly disagrees with reality. When a new technique drops, your first instinct is to ask which Microsoft signal would catch it, and whether customers have it switched on.

You also know Microsoft never sits still. Hunting tables appear, columns get renamed, Graph versions retire, capability shuffles between SKUs, previews go GA, features quietly vanish, and native alert logic shifts underneath you. You've got a repeatable way of staying ahead of that churn instead of finding out when a detection stops firing. You're comfortable behind a command line and in front of a customer, including scenarios where the conversation isn’t pleasant. If that's you, we'd love to talk! We have an amazing team and believe you'll love getting to know us.

At Expel, we help businesses bridge the cybersecurity talent gap by providing transparent Managed Detection and Response. To do this we build technology to make sure our security analysts are solving important problems, and automation is helping them make better decisions at every step. We delight in using technology to make security accessible for our customers.

What Expel can do for you

  • Make you one of our recognized authorities on Microsoft detection and response — for our SOC, our engineers, our go-to-market teams, and our customers
  • Give you real ownership of Expel's detection coverage across the whole Microsoft security estate
  • Put Microsoft telemetry from across our customer base in front of you — a breadth of real-world environments no single enterprise gets to see
  • Let you write and tune detections in our own rule engine and watch them run against live signal
  • Treat AI tooling (Claude Code and friends) as a first-class part of how you work, not a side experiment
  • Enable you to learn from analysts, data scientists, engineers, and responders responsible for various components of Expel's product and services
  • Provide access to popular EDR, network, SIEM, identity, and cloud technologies well beyond the Microsoft stack
  • Challenge you to push the boundaries of our security vision

What you can do for Expel

  • Own our detection coverage across Defender XDR, Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, Azure, and Microsoft 365 — from raw signal through to shipped, tuned detections
  • Build and maintain a living map of Microsoft security signal: what exists, known ingestion lag, where it lands, what gates it, how long it's kept, and how far you can trust it
  • Track how that signal changes and turn every material change into a concrete action — catching drift before it costs us efficacy
  • Tell us where Microsoft's native detections are strong enough to lean on, where they're noisy or shallow, and where Expel needs its own layer
  • Make SOC analysts faster by automating Microsoft-specific investigative workflows against the Graph, Defender, Sentinel, and Entra APIs
  • Partner with Engineering on our Microsoft integrations — ingestion, API limits and throttling, and schema mapping
  • Answer the hard questions from the SOC, CS, and Sales — and mentor the people asking them
  • Help customers understand what they're actually covered for, what they're missing, and what turning it on would buy them

What you should bring with you

  • Deep, current, hands-on knowledge of the Microsoft security stack — Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, Cloud Apps), Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, and the Azure and Microsoft 365 control and data planes
  • Fluency in KQL: you can write, read, optimize, and debug non-trivial hunting queries across both Defender Advanced Hunting and Sentinel, and you know how and why the two schemas differ
  • Working knowledge of the Graph and Graph Security APIs, the Defender and Sentinel APIs, and their authentication, permission, versioning, and throttling models
  • A strong grasp of the Entra ID (and legacy Active Directory) identity attack surface — authentication flows, conditional access, OAuth application consent, token theft and replay, hybrid identity and sync, privileged role abuse — and the telemetry each produces
  • Solid understanding of Windows internals and command line tooling, with enough macOS and Linux to keep up with Defender's cross-platform coverage
  • Experience writing, deploying, and tuning custom detections against Microsoft data sets, plus enough non-Microsoft exposure (AWS, GCP, other EDR and SIEM) to keep perspective
  • Proficiency with Python and Sigma, and real fluency using Anthropic tools such as Claude Code to work across systems and data (locally, via MCP, and so on)
  • 5+ years in information technology or security operations, with substantial time spent defending or operating Microsoft environments
  • Excellent tact and diplomacy skills — you can explain Microsoft's limits to an audience that doesn't want to hear about them
  • SC-200, AZ-500, or SC-300 are a plus; demonstrated depth matters considerably more

Work Location

Our headquarters is in Herndon, Virginia. However, we realize that while there is a benefit to in-person interaction, good people don’t all live in Northern Virginia. Remote work is an option for this role.

Headquarters: San Francisco, US (Remote)

About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com.

About the Team

The Customer Value Architects team sits inside the revenue organization and owns the connection between what customers buy and what they actually get out of Mixpanel. We turn product usage into measurable business outcomes, working across onboarding, adoption, and renewal to make sure customers see the value they signed up for.

About the Role

The right candidate is a relationship-first advisor who connects a customer's Mixpanel investment to real outcomes for a defined book of accounts. You'll own the adoption and value plan for each account end to end: understanding why the customer bought Mixpanel, tracking whether they're getting the ROI they expected, and driving the enablement and product usage that gets them there. You'll build trusted relationships with business and technical stakeholders, partner closely with your Account Executive and renewal counterparts, and bring a growing point of view on how customers should think about AI in their product workflows. This role suits someone who can own a project end to end and is ready to start extending their influence beyond their own accounts to the wider team.

Responsibilities

  • Own the value plan for each account in your portfolio, connecting the business problem that led the customer to buy Mixpanel with the outcomes they measure.
  • Build relationships with business and technical stakeholders, aligning Mixpanel's capabilities to what customers care about most.
  • Run discovery on customer priorities and pain points, and turn what you learn into concrete adoption plans and internal updates.
  • Partner with your Account Executive on expansion and your renewal counterpart on renewal execution, bringing the value case and adoption evidence that supports both.
  • Lead enablement/best practices sessions on dashboard design, funnel analysis, and retention modeling to grow how deeply and widely a customer uses Mixpanel.
  • Monitor usage and health signals and lead business reviews that surface what's working, deepen adoption, and catch risk early.
  • Spot underused features and contracted capabilities, and turn them into clear recommendations for the customer.
  • Triage product questions and issues, solving what you can and routing the rest to the right team.
  • Build a working point of view on a customer's AI maturity, and use Mixpanel's own AI surface to help them build on their product data.
  • Coordinate with GTM, Product, and Engineering on escalations, and share what works with the broader Customer Value Architects team.

We're Looking For Someone Who Has

  • 4 - 6 years of experience in customer success, consulting, or a related field supporting B2B SaaS accounts, or equivalent experience.
  • A track record of managing relationships across a range of stakeholders, from business partners to technical teams.
  • The ability to translate technical concepts, like data models and product metrics, into terms that land with non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience turning product usage into a clear story about customer outcomes and ROI.
  • Comfort building and running adoption plans that tie daily work to a customer's larger goals.
  • Hands-on experience with AI or agentic tooling beyond casual use, such as MCP-based workflows or LLM copilots.
  • A collaborative approach to working across account teams and internal partners to move plans forward.
  • Good judgment for prioritizing which accounts and actions need attention first.

Bonus Points For

  • Background in product analytics, growth, or data-driven product development.
  • Experience in a technical advisory or professional services capacity.
  • Familiarity with analytics instrumentation, event tracking, or data tooling.

#LI-Remote

Compensation

The amount listed below is the total target cash compensation (TTCC) and includes base compensation and variable compensation in the form of either a company bonus or commissions. Variable compensation type is determined by your role and level. In addition to the cash compensation provided, this position is also eligible for equity consideration and other benefits including medical, vision, and dental insurance coverage. You can view our benefits offerings here.

Our salary ranges are determined by role and level and are benchmarked to the SF Bay Area Technology data cut released by Radford, a global compensation database. The range displayed represents the minimum and maximum TTCC for new hire salaries for the position across all of our US locations. To stay on top of market conditions, we refresh our salary ranges twice a year so these ranges may change in the future. Within the range, individual pay is determined by experience, job-related skills, qualifications, and other factors. If you have questions about the specific range, your recruiter can share this information.

$125,500—$169,500 USD

Benefits and Perks

title: Head of Technology
description: Headquarters: New York City URL: https://sanctuary.computer We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code. Original job posting link About garden3d We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions. Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian. We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space. We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs. Sanctuary Computer - Development At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson. Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development. XXIX - Design When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be. We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility. Index - Community Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools. We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care. garden3d TK — Media At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture. We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music. Plus, our partner organizations Lightphone Mill IngredientAI ⛰️ The Head of Technology Role The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it. You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you. This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical. This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them. They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves. They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world. Responsibilities & Mandates ️ Systems that hold up We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out. All in on agentic development The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on. Practical engineering We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay. Code quality at Sanctuary Computer Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.
